models_evaluated: RSL Male Pelvic CT (v1.0.0) Deep Learning Segmentation

links.outcome: Detection of clinically relevant AI errors by comparing AI output with clinician-corrected output
links.effect: Local Surface Dice 0.93±0.11 vs Standard 0.98±0.04 for anorectum (p=0.006); ADD 0.9±0.8 Gy anorectum D1cm3; combined metrics detected clinically relevant changes
links.quote: Combining dose-volume and geometrical metrics allowed detection of clinically relevant changes, applied to both auto-segmentation and auto-planning output and the Local Surface Dice was more sensitive to local changes compared to the Standard Surface Dice.

links.outcome: Differences between vendor training data and local deployment population volumes
links.effect: PTV 154±45 vs 120±50 cm3, bladder 141±51 vs 226±136 cm3, rectum 58±18 vs 76±29 cm3 (all p<0.001), training vs local
links.quote: The geometrical analysis showed significant volume differences between the training and the local dataset for respectively PTV ((154 ± 45)cm 3 ; (120 ± 50)cm 3 with p < 0.001), bladder ((141 ± 51)cm 3 ; (226 ± 136)cm 3 with p < 0.001) and rectum ((58 ± 18)cm 3 ; (76 ± 29)cm 3 with p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Clinical goal fulfillment of AI plans vs clinician-reviewed/optimized plans
links.effect: AI plans met all mandatory goals in 90% vs 100% after clinician review; optimal goals 32% vs 74%
links.quote: Clinical goal evaluation revealed that P DL did fulfill all mandatory clinical goals ( Table 1 ) in 90 % of the cases, while all where fulfilled in P clin .

unlisted_practices: Use of monitoring metrics to select out-of-distribution cases as candidates for active learning/model retraining

links.outcome: Clinical goal fulfillment before and after clinician review and plan optimization
links.effect: Mandatory clinical goals were fulfilled in 90 % of AI plans and all clinically approved plans; optimal constraints in 32 % and 74 %, respectively.
links.quote: Clinical goal evaluation revealed that P DL did fulfill all mandatory clinical goals ( Table 1 ) in 90 % of the cases, while all where fulfilled in P clin .

links.outcome: Sensitivity of monitoring metrics to clinically relevant segmentation corrections
links.effect: Local versus Standard Surface Dice: anorectum (0.93 ± 0.11) versus (0.98 ± 0.04), p = 0.006; bladder (0.97 ± 0.06) versus (0.98 ± 0.04), p = 0.3.
links.quote: The Standard Surface Dice 3 mm and the Local Surface Dice 3 mm reported values of (0.98 ± 0.04) and (0.93 ± 0.11) (p = 0.006) respectively for the anorectum, and (0.98 ± 0.04) and (0.97 ± 0.06) (p = 0.3) for bladder.

links.outcome: Detection of out-of-distribution planning inputs using volume and clinical-goal analysis
links.effect: Training versus local volumes: PTV (154 ± 45)cm 3 versus (120 ± 50)cm 3; bladder (141 ± 51)cm 3 versus (226 ± 136)cm 3; both p < 0.001.
links.quote: The geometrical analysis showed significant volume differences between the training and the local dataset for respectively PTV ((154 ± 45)cm 3 ; (120 ± 50)cm 3 with p < 0.001), bladder ((141 ± 51)cm 3 ; (226 ± 136)cm 3 with p < 0.001) and rectum ((58 ± 18)cm 3 ; (76 ± 29)cm 3 with p < 0.001).

links.outcome: volume differences between training and local data
links.effect: Significant volume differences were observed between the training dataset and the local dataset for the PTV, bladder, and rectum.
links.quote: The geometrical analysis showed significant volume differences between the training and the local dataset for respectively PTV ((154 ± 45)cm3; (120 ± 50)cm3 with p < 0.001), bladder ((141 ± 51)cm3; (226 ± 136)cm3 with p < 0.001) and rectum ((58 ± 18)cm3; (76 ± 29)cm3 with p < 0.001).

links.outcome: detection of clinically relevant AI performance changes
links.effect: Comparing AI outputs against clinically approved structures using combined dose-volume and geometrical metrics successfully detected clinically relevant changes for monitoring.
links.quote: Combining dose-volume and geometrical metrics allowed detection of clinically relevant changes, applied to both auto-segmentation and auto-planning output and the Local Surface Dice was more sensitive to local changes compared to the Standard Surface Dice.

unlisted_practices: Using combined geometrical and dose-volume metrics for continuous performance monitoring of auto-segmentation and auto-planning models

screen.practice: performance monitoring with geometric and dose-volume metrics
screen.reason: The study empirically tests a post-deployment quality assurance/performance monitoring method (using combined geometrical and dose-volume metrics) to detect clinically relevant AI failures and identify candidates for model retraining.
